chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Salamah, from al-Husayn ibn Yusuf, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hajjaj al-Khashshab, from Abu al-Fawaris, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) forbade me from speaking between the four rak'ahs that are after the Maghrib prayer.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on speaking during the four rak'ahs after Maghrib?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Imam’s emphasis on khushu’ (devotional focus) by prohibiting speech during the intervals of the four supererogatory rak'ahs following Maghrib. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the distinction between mere ritual performance and the spiritual presence of heart, ensuring that the time between units remains dedicated to remembrance rather than worldly discourse. It reflects the broader scholarly principle that the quality of worship is as critical as its quantity, particularly in voluntary acts of devotion.
